# Adjudication Task — Chapter 181

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃181화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“너는 잠시라도 눈을 뗐다 하면 사고를 치는구나.”
  6|
  7|가볍게 사제를 꾸짖은 백무성이 우황태를 향해 고개를 숙여 보였다.
  8|
  9|“서로 간에 사소한 오해가 있었던 것 같습니다. 넓은 아량으로 용서하시지요.”
 10|
 11|인상만큼이나 부드러운 목소리였다.
 12|
 13|우황태는 무인이라기보다는 장사치에 가까웠다. 무공은 일류지만 표국을 운영해 오며 길러 낸 눈썰미만큼은 절정이라고 자부할 수 있을 만큼.
 14|
 15|아마 평소였다면 백무성을 본 순간 이런 생각을 했을지도 모른다.
 16|
 17|‘평범 속의 비범.’
 18|
 19|그러나 불행히도 지금의 우황태는 제정신이 아니었다.
 20|
 21|난데없이 끼어든 백무성의 멀끔한 인상은 만만해 보였고 공손하면서도 강자의 여유가 묻어 나오는 목소리는 건방지게만 들렸다.
 22|
 23|“뭐라, 넓은 아량으로 용서?”
 24|
 25|부글거리는 목소리로 뇌까린 그가 눈썹을 치켜떴다.
 26|
 27|“감히 누구한테 이래라저래라 하는 것이냐?”
 28|
 29|“그런 의도로 드린 말씀은 아닙니다만, 마음이 상하셨다면 사과드리지요.”
 30|
 31|“사과? 허, 이 하룻강아지 같은 놈이 그래도.”
 32|
 33|까드득.
 34|
 35|본래 한 번 분노에 사로잡히면 사고가 흐려지기 마련.
 36|
 37|주먹을 말아 쥐며 나서는 우황태를 다른 문주들이 황급히 만류했다.
 38|
 39|“우 국주, 이쯤에서 그만하는 것이 좋겠소.”
 40|
 41|“송 문주의 말이 옳소이다. 괜히 소란 일으켜 봤자 좋을 게 뭐가 있겠소?”
 42|
 43|“어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지 모를 놈들이 건방을 떠는데 참아라? 당신들도 나를 우습게 여기는 거요?”
 44|
 45|“아니, 그 말이 아니라.”
 46|
 47|“그럼 무슨 말이 하고 싶은 건가?”
 48|
 49|이제는 반쯤 하대나 다름없는 말투. 산서오문의 문주들은 내심 눈살을 찌푸렸지만 괜한 분란은 막아야 했다.
 50|
 51|“그저 시기와 장소가 틀렸다는 말이오. 우리 처지를 잊은 거요?”
 52|
 53|“굳이 하겠다면 더 이상 말리지는 않겠소만…… 태원진가에 미운털이 박힌 이때 소란을 일으킬 필요는 없지.”
 54|
 55|“화난 건 이해하지만 우리 입장도 생각해 주시구려. 다 같이 좀 살아 봅시다.”
 56|
 57|또, 또. 그놈의 태원진가!
 58|
 59|우황태는 순간 터져 나오려는 욕설을 가까스로 참았다. 주위에 수많은 눈과 귀가 없었다면 온갖 욕설을 퍼부으며 눈에 보이는 것들을 전부 때려 부쉈을 것이다.
 60|
 61|하지만 마지막 한 줄기 이성이 그를 붙잡았다.
 62|
 63|“끄으으응.”
 64|
 65|간신히 마음을 진정시킨 우황태가 백무성을 노려보았다. 그는 여전히 침착한 표정으로 그 자리에 서 있었다.
 66|
 67|“마음 같아서는 당장 단매에 때려죽여도 시원치 않지만…… 촌무지렁이의 실수라 생각하고 넘어가 주마. 꺼져라, 마음이 바뀌기 전에.”
 68|
 69|물끄러미 그를 바라보던 백무성이 고개를 숙였다.
 70|
 71|“사정을 봐주셔서 감사드립니다.”
 72|
 73|“흥, 운 좋은 놈들.”
 74|
 75|그러나 운이 좋은 것은 우황태였다.
 76|
 77|백무성이 한발 앞서 전음을 날리지 않았더라면 그는 지금쯤 사경을 헤매고 있었을 테니까.
 78|
 79|- 둘째, 멈춰라.
 80|
 81|막 몸을 날리려던 매화삼절의 둘째, 패화권(敗華拳) 철우의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 82|
 83|그의 잇새 사이로 다른 이에게 들리지 않는 음성이 새어 나왔다.
 84|
 85|- 저로 모자라서 대사형까지 건드린 놈입니다.
 86|
 87|- 상관없다.
 88|
 89|- 전 상관있습니다. 한 대만, 딱 한 대만 때리면 안 됩니까?
 90|
 91|- 때려죽이고 싶다는 말로 들리는구나.
 92|
 93|- ……살살 때리겠습니다. 진짜 딱 한 대만요.
 94|
 95|- 그건 살살 때려죽이겠다는 말이고. 괜한 시선을 끌지 말라는 사부님의 엄명을 잊었느냐?
 96|
 97|갈등하던 철우가 꽉 움켜쥐고 있던 주먹을 늘어뜨렸다.
 98|
 99|“후우, 미치겠네.”
100|
101|백무성이 대견하다는 듯 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
102|
103|“잘 참았다. 이 또한 수련이다.”
104|
105|“이게 뭐가 수련입니까? 기껏 배워 놓은 무공도 제때 못 쓰는구먼.”
106|
107|“무분별한 살생(殺生)은 너를 망칠 뿐이다. 무공은 정기신을 갈고 닦는 것이지, 누군가를 죽이기 위한 게 아니야.”
108|
109|“사형을 볼 때마다 헷갈립니다. 제가 화산파 제자인지, 소림사 승려인지.”
110|
111|“네 녀석 성격에 승려가 가당키나 하겠느냐? 앞으로 부숴 먹을 목탁만 불쌍하지.”
112|
113|피식 웃는 백무성의 모습에 철우가 한숨을 내쉬었다.
114|
115|마음 깊이 존경하는 사형이지만 너무 사람이 좋아서 문제다.
116|
117|“저런 놈들은 아구창을 박살 내야 하는 건데…….”
118|
119|“어허, 그 입!”
120|
121|“알겠습니다. 알겠어요.”
122|
123|철우는 어느새 훌쩍 멀어진 우황태의 뒷모습을 바라보며 입맛을 다셨다.
124|
125|‘얼굴 기억해 뒀다. 한 번만 걸려라.’
126|
127|그런 사제의 생각을 모를 리 없는 백무성이다. 그는 고개를 절레절레 내저었다.
128|
129|“허튼 생각은 그만하고 막내부터 찾거라.”
130|
131|“은향이 그 녀석 또 없어졌습니까?”
132|
133|“그래, 너처럼 말이지.”
134|
135|철우가 움찔했다.
136|
137|“저, 저는 소피보러 간 겁니다.”
138|
139|“그랬지. 그런데 소피보러 간다는 놈이 왜 사람 많은 곳에서 시비가 붙었느냐?”
140|
141|“시원하게 비우고 오는 길에 그만. 아니 사형, 지금 저 못 믿으시는 겁니까? 아직 손 안 닦았는데 냄새 맡아 보실래요?”
142|
143|“……됐다.”
144|
145|백무성은 관자놀이를 문질렀다. 누구보다 아끼는 사제들이지만 다루기가 여간 까다로운 것이 아니었다.
146|
147|그나마 철우는 덩치라도 커서 금방 찾지, 막내 사제인 은향은 이런 인파 속에서 보이지도 않는다.
148|
149|“보이는 것 없느냐?”
150|
151|남들보다 머리 두 개는 더 큰 철우가 주위를 쓱 훑었다.
152|
153|“글쎄요. 사람이 워낙 많아서.”
154|
155|끝도 없이 늘어선 북적이는 인파 속에서 자그마한 체구의 소녀를 찾는 건 절정 고수의 눈으로도 어렵다.
156|
157|오죽 사람이 많으면 곳곳에 좌판을 깐 장사치들마저 보일 정도였다.
158|
159|“그나저나 태원진가가 이 정도였습니까? 오기 전까지는 들어 본 적도 없는데.”
160|
161|“아는 사람은 알지. 현 문주인 산서기협(山西奇俠)도 그렇고, 진천검(振天劍)도 제법 알려져 있지 않느냐?”
162|
163|“산서기협은 잘 모르겠고 진천검이라면 십봉룡이니 뭐니 하는 그놈 말입니까?”
164|
165|“그놈이라니. 입조심하거라.”
166|
167|“학관이나 다니는 샌님인데요, 뭘. 제 생각엔 아마 대사형이 훨씬…….”
168|
169|“어허. 보기도 전에 사람을 판단하는 고약한 버릇은 어디서 배웠느냐? 그는 분명 뛰어난 인재다.”
170|
171|“뭐, 산서성에서 그 정도면 개천에서 용 난 것이나 다름없긴 합니다만.”
172|
173|시큰둥하게 대꾸하던 철우가 문득 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
174|
175|“그 왜, 진천검 말고도 무슨 용인지 미꾸라지인지, 한 명 더 있지 않습니까?”
176|
177|“용? 산서잠룡을 말하는 것이냐?”
178|
179|“아, 맞습니다. 산서잠룡.”
180|
181|“진천검만큼은 아니지만 제법 뛰어난 기재라고 들었지.”
182|
183|“용인지 미꾸라진지, 오는 길에 지긋지긋하게 들어서 얼굴이나 한번 봐야겠습니다.”
184|
185|주먹을 불끈 움켜쥐는 철우를 본 백무성의 입꼬리가 슬쩍 올라갔다.
186|
187|“겨뤄 보고 싶으냐?”
188|
189|철우가 뒤통수를 긁적이며 대답했다.
190|
191|“뭐, 꼭 그런 건 아닙니다. 어차피 제가 이길 건데.”
192|
193|“호승심은 좋다만 분란은 가급적 피해야 한다.”
194|
195|“분란 일으킬 거리나 있겠습니까? 기왕 나온 김에 실력이나 보자는 거지.”
196|
197|백무성은 둘째 사제를 지그시 응시했다.
198|
199|말과는 달리 제법 궁금한 기색이 역력하다.
200|
201|철우의 성격에 몇 년째 화산에 틀어박혀 매일 같은 이들만 상대하다 보니 들뜬 모양이었다.
202|
203|“금방 볼 수 있을 게다. 물론 그전에 막내를 찾아야겠지만.”
204|
205|뒤에 덧붙인 말은 한숨에 가까웠다.
206|
207|이미 태원진가의 문은 열렸고 초대받은 이들이 구름처럼 몰려간 상황이다.
208|
209|그가 나무에라도 올라가야 하나 고민하던 그때였다.
210|
211|“사형, 조금 시끄러운 건 괜찮지 않습니까?”
212|
213|“뭐?”
214|
215|씩 웃어 보인 철우가 크게 숨을 들이켰다.
216|
217|그리고 다음 순간, 천둥 같은 외침이 터져 나왔다.
218|
219|“은-향-아!!!”
220|
221|미처 말릴 새도 없었다. 철우의 목청은 체구만큼이나 대단했다.
222|
223|그들의 주위에 있던 사람들은 귀를 막으며 주저앉았고, 웃고 떠들던 수많은 사람이 입을 닫았다.
224|
225|찬물이라도 끼얹은 듯 모두가 침묵한 그때였다.
226|
227|“오라버니들! 나 여기!”
228|
229|저 멀리, 제자리에서 열심히 깡충깡충 뛰고 있는 한 소녀를 발견한 철우가 의기양양하게 말했다.
230|
231|“으하하! 사형, 찾았습니다!”
232|
233|“……그래, 잘했다. 아주 잘했어.”
234|
235|백무성이 머리를 짚은 그때였다.
236|
237|쏴아아아.
238|
239|마치 바람에 갈대밭이 갈라지듯 수백 명의 사람들이 웅성거리며 길을 텄다.
240|
241|그리고 그 끝에 철탑처럼 서 있는 한 사내를 본 철우가 자신도 모르게 중얼거렸다.
242|
243|“저게 사람이야, 곰이야.”
244|
245|“사람이다. 그가 아니었다면 오늘의 태원진가도 없었겠지.”
246|
247|곰 같은 사내, 진위경을 향해 백무성은 공손히 포권을 취했다.
248|
249|
250|
251|* * *
252|
253|
254|
255|두두두두!
256|
257|풍경이 휙휙 스쳐 지나간다. 바로 옆에서 말을 몰고 있던 혁무진이 소리치듯 외쳤다.
258|
259|“분명히 갈 때는 느렸는데, 돌아올 때는 엄청 빠르네요. 이틀 전에는 좀 느긋하게 가서 그런가?”
260|
261|“모든 일에는 다 이유가 있지.”
262|
263|“무슨 이유요?”
264|
265|“누군가가 말을 타면서 뭔가를 처먹으려고 시도하지 않으면 돼. 그럼 빨라져.”
266|
267|“아.”
268|
269|청풍은 시종일관 우울한 표정이었다. 출발 전, 음식을 잔뜩 포장하려는 녀석을 내가 제지했기 때문이었다.
270|
271|“배고파요.”
272|
273|나는 냉정하게 대꾸했다.
274|
275|“참으세요.”
276|
277|절정 고수는 소화력도 절정이더라. 청풍은 먹는 만큼 많이 쌌고, 싼 만큼 도로 처먹었다.
278|
279|거기에 더해 자주 먹으니 자주 쌀 수밖에…… 젠장, 더러워서 여기까지 해야겠다.
280|
281|“어디까지 왔냐?”
282|
283|“방금 지나친 게 아홉 번째 마을이니까…… 짧으면 반 시진, 길면 한 시진 안에 도착할 것 같은데요.”
284|
285|쏟아지는 햇살에 눈이 따갑다. 나는 중천을 향해 슬금슬금 올라가는 태양을 바라봤다.
286|
287|“도착하면 정오 쯤 되려나.”
288|
289|“아마도요.”
290|
291|“늦었겠지?”
292|
293|“그야 당연히 늦었죠. 조금 덜 늦으려고 불나게 뛰는 것 아니겠습니까.”
294|
295|그건 그래.
296|
297|나는 대답 대신 말에 박차를 가했다. 달릴 때마다 등에 메어 놓은 길쭉한 보퉁이가 말 등을 때린다.
298|
299|‘어우, 성가셔 죽겠네.’
300|
301|보퉁이에 든 것은 [이름 없는 검]이다.
302|

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“We were definitely slow on the way there, but we’re incredibly fast coming back. Is it because we took our time two days ago?”

[P129]
“Everything happens for a reason.”

[P130]
“What reason?”

[P131]
“We move faster when no one tries to stuff his face while riding a horse.”

[P132]
“Ah.”

[P133]
Cheongpung had looked gloomy the entire trip. Before we left, I had stopped him from packing a mountain of food.

[P134]
“I’m hungry.”

[P135]
I answered coldly.

[P136]
“Endure it.”

[P137]
A Peak master’s digestion was Peak-level too. Cheongpung crapped as much as he ate, then ate as much as he crapped.

[P138]
And since he ate often, he naturally had to crap often…

[P139]
Damn it. This is disgusting. I’ll stop there.

[P140]
“How far are we?”

[P141]
“We just passed the ninth village, so… We should arrive in half a shichen at the earliest, or one full shichen at the latest.”

[P142]
The sunlight pouring down made my eyes sting. I looked up at the sun as it slowly climbed toward the middle of the sky.

[P143]
“So we’ll arrive around noon?”

[P144]
“Probably.”

[P145]
“We’re late, aren’t we?”

[P146]
“Of course we’re late. Isn’t that why we’re riding like hell, trying to be a little less late?”

[P147]
Fair point.

[P148]
Instead of answering, I spurred my horse onward. With every stride, the long bundle strapped across my back thumped against the horse’s back.

[P149]
*Ugh, what a pain.*

[P150]
The bundle contained the Unnamed Sword.

[P151]
I was supposed to have returned it to Jeok Cheongang, but instead, I had somehow ended up taking it back.

[P152]
As long as I lived in a Murim where the law was damn far away and fists were painfully close, I didn’t have much of a choice.

[P153]
*It’s not like I can put it in my inventory either.*

[P154]
I could at least claim I had tucked the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual inside my clothes. But if an entire sword suddenly popped out of my pocket, there would be no explaining that away.

[P155]
If I were alone, it might be different. But with other people watching, it would be the perfect way to get accused of practicing demonic, heterodox arts.

[P156]
*I really got myself into a mess this time.*

[P157]
It wasn’t that I resented being saddled with a troublesome object. I simply hated the thought of having to meet Fire King Jeok Cheongang—that terrifying old man—again.

[P158]
*Let’s meet again soon.*

[P159]
*Meet again, my ass.*

[P160]
Every time I remembered what he had said a few shichen ago, my stomach churned.

[P161]
Hyuk Mujin, who had been sneaking glances at me, finally asked,

[P162]
“Why do you look like that?”

[P163]
“I was thinking about the Fire King.”

[P164]
“Ugh. Life’s too short for anything but happy thoughts, so why imagine something that horrible?”

[P165]
“If you were me, wouldn’t you think about him? He said he’d be back soon.”

[P166]
“Speaking of which, could you give me some time off? I suddenly miss my family.”

[P167]
“You bastard. You’re trying to save yourself.”

[P168]
“You never know what might happen. Before I die, I should at least see my parents’ faces one more time.”

[P169]
“That doesn’t sound like something an unfilial son who hasn’t shown his face in years should say.”

[P170]
“I’d like to take this opportunity to become a good son.”

[P171]
“Nope.”

[P172]
I dismissed Hyuk Mujin’s bullshit and looked up at the sky with a sigh.

[P173]
“Even the heavens are heartless. Why did that old man have to leave this thing with me?”

[P174]
“He said it was a pain to carry around.”

[P175]
“For such a stupid reason?”

[P176]
“With him, I can completely believe it.”

[P177]
“…”

[P178]
That was surprisingly convincing.

[P179]
“I could lose it before he comes back. Or I could quietly pocket it for myself.”

[P180]
“You, Captain?”

[P181]
Hyuk Mujin laughed as though he had just heard the funniest joke in the world.

[P182]
“If you were that kind of person, what have you been doing all this time? If you hadn’t been on the verge of death, you probably would’ve just kept the Blazing Flame Divine Pill too.”

[P183]
“That’s…”

[P184]
He had a point.

[P185]
“Just hide it somewhere no one will find it. Who knows? Maybe the great Fire King will teach you a move as thanks.”

[P186]
“Teach me, my ass. I’m sure he’d love to teach the man who killed his Disciple.”

[P187]
The absurdity drew a quiet laugh from me.

[P188]
The Fire Gate Clan was said to pass its arts down to a single successor and never teach outsiders. Even setting personal feelings aside, the idea that he would teach martial arts to an outsider like me was ridiculous.

[P189]
“Your nonsense is only funny in moderation, you idiot.”

[P190]
“Well, now that you mention it, I suppose you’re right.”

[P191]
At that moment, Cheongpung—who had been drooping like a corpse and endlessly repeating that he was hungry—spoke up.

[P192]
“Isn’t he trying to take you as his Disciple, Benefactor?”

[P193]
“…”

[P194]
“…”

[P195]
“Maybe not? I think he is. Grandpa Jeok seemed to be watching you closely, Benefactor.”

[P196]
“Me?”

[P197]
“Captain?”

[P198]
Our gazes met in midair. Hyuk Mujin looked utterly baffled. I was probably making the same face.

[P199]
We both let out disbelieving laughs.

[P200]
“That’s great. Congratulations in advance, Captain.”

[P201]
“Yeah. Thanks.”

[P202]
*Me? Someone he’d known for barely a day or two?*

[P203]
The idea was so absurd it didn’t even qualify as a joke.

[P204]
“Maybe not? Or am I right?”

[P205]
As Cheongpung tilted his head over his own bizarre suggestion, Hyuk Mujin raised a finger and pointed into the distance.

[P206]
“Can you see it?”

[P207]
I could.

[P208]
People were walking down a well-kept road. Farther ahead lay a broad expanse of land surrounded by a teeming crowd.

[P209]
*The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

[P210]
I was back after three days away.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 181

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃181화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“너는 잠시라도 눈을 뗐다 하면 사고를 치는구나.”
  6|
  7|가볍게 사제를 꾸짖은 백무성이 우황태를 향해 고개를 숙여 보였다.
  8|
  9|“서로 간에 사소한 오해가 있었던 것 같습니다. 넓은 아량으로 용서하시지요.”
 10|
 11|인상만큼이나 부드러운 목소리였다.
 12|
 13|우황태는 무인이라기보다는 장사치에 가까웠다. 무공은 일류지만 표국을 운영해 오며 길러 낸 눈썰미만큼은 절정이라고 자부할 수 있을 만큼.
 14|
 15|아마 평소였다면 백무성을 본 순간 이런 생각을 했을지도 모른다.
 16|
 17|‘평범 속의 비범.’
 18|
 19|그러나 불행히도 지금의 우황태는 제정신이 아니었다.
 20|
 21|난데없이 끼어든 백무성의 멀끔한 인상은 만만해 보였고 공손하면서도 강자의 여유가 묻어 나오는 목소리는 건방지게만 들렸다.
 22|
 23|“뭐라, 넓은 아량으로 용서?”
 24|
 25|부글거리는 목소리로 뇌까린 그가 눈썹을 치켜떴다.
 26|
 27|“감히 누구한테 이래라저래라 하는 것이냐?”
 28|
 29|“그런 의도로 드린 말씀은 아닙니다만, 마음이 상하셨다면 사과드리지요.”
 30|
 31|“사과? 허, 이 하룻강아지 같은 놈이 그래도.”
 32|
 33|까드득.
 34|
 35|본래 한 번 분노에 사로잡히면 사고가 흐려지기 마련.
 36|
 37|주먹을 말아 쥐며 나서는 우황태를 다른 문주들이 황급히 만류했다.
 38|
 39|“우 국주, 이쯤에서 그만하는 것이 좋겠소.”
 40|
 41|“송 문주의 말이 옳소이다. 괜히 소란 일으켜 봤자 좋을 게 뭐가 있겠소?”
 42|
 43|“어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지 모를 놈들이 건방을 떠는데 참아라? 당신들도 나를 우습게 여기는 거요?”
 44|
 45|“아니, 그 말이 아니라.”
 46|
 47|“그럼 무슨 말이 하고 싶은 건가?”
 48|
 49|이제는 반쯤 하대나 다름없는 말투. 산서오문의 문주들은 내심 눈살을 찌푸렸지만 괜한 분란은 막아야 했다.
 50|
 51|“그저 시기와 장소가 틀렸다는 말이오. 우리 처지를 잊은 거요?”
 52|
 53|“굳이 하겠다면 더 이상 말리지는 않겠소만…… 태원진가에 미운털이 박힌 이때 소란을 일으킬 필요는 없지.”
 54|
 55|“화난 건 이해하지만 우리 입장도 생각해 주시구려. 다 같이 좀 살아 봅시다.”
 56|
 57|또, 또. 그놈의 태원진가!
 58|
 59|우황태는 순간 터져 나오려는 욕설을 가까스로 참았다. 주위에 수많은 눈과 귀가 없었다면 온갖 욕설을 퍼부으며 눈에 보이는 것들을 전부 때려 부쉈을 것이다.
 60|
 61|하지만 마지막 한 줄기 이성이 그를 붙잡았다.
 62|
 63|“끄으으응.”
 64|
 65|간신히 마음을 진정시킨 우황태가 백무성을 노려보았다. 그는 여전히 침착한 표정으로 그 자리에 서 있었다.
 66|
 67|“마음 같아서는 당장 단매에 때려죽여도 시원치 않지만…… 촌무지렁이의 실수라 생각하고 넘어가 주마. 꺼져라, 마음이 바뀌기 전에.”
 68|
 69|물끄러미 그를 바라보던 백무성이 고개를 숙였다.
 70|
 71|“사정을 봐주셔서 감사드립니다.”
 72|
 73|“흥, 운 좋은 놈들.”
 74|
 75|그러나 운이 좋은 것은 우황태였다.
 76|
 77|백무성이 한발 앞서 전음을 날리지 않았더라면 그는 지금쯤 사경을 헤매고 있었을 테니까.
 78|
 79|- 둘째, 멈춰라.
 80|
 81|막 몸을 날리려던 매화삼절의 둘째, 패화권(敗華拳) 철우의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 82|
 83|그의 잇새 사이로 다른 이에게 들리지 않는 음성이 새어 나왔다.
 84|
 85|- 저로 모자라서 대사형까지 건드린 놈입니다.
 86|
 87|- 상관없다.
 88|
 89|- 전 상관있습니다. 한 대만, 딱 한 대만 때리면 안 됩니까?
 90|
 91|- 때려죽이고 싶다는 말로 들리는구나.
 92|
 93|- ……살살 때리겠습니다. 진짜 딱 한 대만요.
 94|
 95|- 그건 살살 때려죽이겠다는 말이고. 괜한 시선을 끌지 말라는 사부님의 엄명을 잊었느냐?
 96|
 97|갈등하던 철우가 꽉 움켜쥐고 있던 주먹을 늘어뜨렸다.
 98|
 99|“후우, 미치겠네.”
100|
101|백무성이 대견하다는 듯 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
102|
103|“잘 참았다. 이 또한 수련이다.”
104|
105|“이게 뭐가 수련입니까? 기껏 배워 놓은 무공도 제때 못 쓰는구먼.”
106|
107|“무분별한 살생(殺生)은 너를 망칠 뿐이다. 무공은 정기신을 갈고 닦는 것이지, 누군가를 죽이기 위한 게 아니야.”
108|
109|“사형을 볼 때마다 헷갈립니다. 제가 화산파 제자인지, 소림사 승려인지.”
110|
111|“네 녀석 성격에 승려가 가당키나 하겠느냐? 앞으로 부숴 먹을 목탁만 불쌍하지.”
112|
113|피식 웃는 백무성의 모습에 철우가 한숨을 내쉬었다.
114|
115|마음 깊이 존경하는 사형이지만 너무 사람이 좋아서 문제다.
116|
117|“저런 놈들은 아구창을 박살 내야 하는 건데…….”
118|
119|“어허, 그 입!”
120|
121|“알겠습니다. 알겠어요.”
122|
123|철우는 어느새 훌쩍 멀어진 우황태의 뒷모습을 바라보며 입맛을 다셨다.
124|
125|‘얼굴 기억해 뒀다. 한 번만 걸려라.’
126|
127|그런 사제의 생각을 모를 리 없는 백무성이다. 그는 고개를 절레절레 내저었다.
128|
129|“허튼 생각은 그만하고 막내부터 찾거라.”
130|
131|“은향이 그 녀석 또 없어졌습니까?”
132|
133|“그래, 너처럼 말이지.”
134|
135|철우가 움찔했다.
136|
137|“저, 저는 소피보러 간 겁니다.”
138|
139|“그랬지. 그런데 소피보러 간다는 놈이 왜 사람 많은 곳에서 시비가 붙었느냐?”
140|
141|“시원하게 비우고 오는 길에 그만. 아니 사형, 지금 저 못 믿으시는 겁니까? 아직 손 안 닦았는데 냄새 맡아 보실래요?”
142|
143|“……됐다.”
144|
145|백무성은 관자놀이를 문질렀다. 누구보다 아끼는 사제들이지만 다루기가 여간 까다로운 것이 아니었다.
146|
147|그나마 철우는 덩치라도 커서 금방 찾지, 막내 사제인 은향은 이런 인파 속에서 보이지도 않는다.
148|
149|“보이는 것 없느냐?”
150|
151|남들보다 머리 두 개는 더 큰 철우가 주위를 쓱 훑었다.
152|
153|“글쎄요. 사람이 워낙 많아서.”
154|
155|끝도 없이 늘어선 북적이는 인파 속에서 자그마한 체구의 소녀를 찾는 건 절정 고수의 눈으로도 어렵다.
156|
157|오죽 사람이 많으면 곳곳에 좌판을 깐 장사치들마저 보일 정도였다.
158|
159|“그나저나 태원진가가 이 정도였습니까? 오기 전까지는 들어 본 적도 없는데.”
160|
161|“아는 사람은 알지. 현 문주인 산서기협(山西奇俠)도 그렇고, 진천검(振天劍)도 제법 알려져 있지 않느냐?”
162|
163|“산서기협은 잘 모르겠고 진천검이라면 십봉룡이니 뭐니 하는 그놈 말입니까?”
164|
165|“그놈이라니. 입조심하거라.”
166|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
